name: npc
entries: Mara Venn, a one-eyed courier who knows every shortcut, refuses to carry weapons, and is secretly transporting a dragon egg.
Brother Caldus, a cheerful healer whose miracles work but whose god officially denies knowing him.
Iri Quickchalk, a goblin cartographer who maps rumors rather than roads and becomes offended when either proves inaccurate.
Lady Seraphine Vale, an impeccably polite noble funding both sides of a rebellion to minimize civilian casualties.
Tomas Rook, a retired monster hunter who now runs a bakery and recognizes the party's flour as mimic dust.
Nella Brass, a young runesmith capable of brilliant work only while someone tells her a completely new story.
Captain Orro Flint, a river-orc guard who loves procedure, competitive poetry, and arresting corrupt superiors.
Velvet, a masked information broker who accepts embarrassing truths as payment and never asks for money.
Old Fen, a shepherd whose sheep predict the weather, danger, and occasionally political assassinations.
Professor Holloway, a spectral historian possessing their own skeleton to continue field research.
Kesh of Seven Knives, an intimidating mercenary who uses six knives for cooking and fears drawing the seventh.
Pella Sunward, a relentlessly optimistic paladin whose holy order was invented during a tavern argument.
Dorrin Slate, a dwarven appraiser who can identify any artifact but compulsively undervalues objects he personally likes.
Mina Thrice-Lost, an explorer who has escaped the same impossible ruin three times and desperately wants to return.
Constable Reed, an honest village officer overwhelmed by crimes involving magic that local law does not acknowledge.
Sable-of-the-Reeds, a marshscale diplomat who pauses for minutes before every answer and never wastes a word.
King Pip IX, a self-proclaimed rat monarch commanding an excellent spy network beneath the capital.
Auntie Ember, an elderly ashborn innkeeper who gives free rooms to adventurers and invoices them later in favors.
Elias North, a charming thief who steals only keys and has no idea what half of them open.
Juniper Wake, a botanist slowly turning into a tree and treating the transformation as a fascinating inconvenience.
The Gray Witness, a silent armored figure appearing near historic events and sketching everyone present.
Nox Bellweather, a fortune-teller whose false predictions are comforting and whose true ones sound absurd.
Rill, a tidekin salvager carrying love letters recovered from wrecks and trying to deliver each one.
Magistrate Odo Penn, a bureaucrat whose enchanted stamp makes ridiculous temporary laws physically real.
Vexa Coil, an alchemist selling reliable potions in reused bottles with dangerously incorrect labels.
Sir Candlewick, a tiny animated suit of armor searching for a person large enough to be its squire.
Hara Moonclaw, a bounty hunter who always offers targets one fair chance to explain themselves.
Merrit Glass, a nervous royal impersonator who has been ruling more competently than the missing monarch.
Sister Quiet, a priest who took a vow of silence and employs three talkative ravens as theological assistants.
Bramble Jack, a friendly bandit leader who insists every robbery include refreshments and a written customer survey.
